title: Mayer-Vietoris sequences are compatible with pullback
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $X=U\cup V$ a union of two open subschemes, and $U'=g^{-1}(U)$, $V'=g^{-1}(V)$, so $Y=U'\cup V'$ and $U'\cap V'=g^{-1}(U\cap V)$; for $W\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}$ write $W'=g^{-1}(W)$ and $g_W:W'\to W$ for the restriction of $g$. Let $\mathcal G$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then the pullback maps of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], $g^*:H^q(X_{\Et},\mathcal G)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},g^{-1}\mathcal G)$ and $g_W^*:H^q(W_{\Et},\mathcal G|_W)\to H^q(W'_{\Et},g_W^{-1}(\mathcal G|_W))\cong H^q(W'_{\Et},(g^{-1}\mathcal G)|_{W'})$ (the identification being $H^q$ of the isomorphism $g_W^{-1}j_W^{-1}\cong j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], both sides being inverse images along $g\circ j_{W'}=j_W\circ g_W$), form a morphism from the Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] for $(X,U,V,\mathcal G)$ to the one for $(Y,U',V',g^{-1}\mathcal G)$: every square, including those with the connecting maps $\delta$, commutes.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50 (lemma-mayer-vietoris) and its proof (the short exact sequences $0\to\mathcal I^\bullet(X)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(U)\oplus\mathcal I^\bullet(V)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V)\to0$ of an injective resolution); the compatibility with pullback is not stated in the source (agent-identified gap: it is needed for the reduction of Theorem 09YQ to the affine case)

proof.text: *Resolutions, and $g^*$ on the chain level.* Choose an injective resolution $s:\mathcal G\to I^\bullet$ on $X_{\Et}$ and an injective resolution $s':g^{-1}\mathcal G\to J^\bullet$ on $Y_{\Et}$, with $I^n=J^n=0$ for $n<0$ ($\Ab(X_{\Et})$, $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]; [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1)); both are K-injective resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] (2). By the independence of the resolution in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] (step 7 of its proof), the Mayer-Vietoris sequence of $(X,U,V,\mathcal G)$ may be computed from $I^\bullet$ and that of $(Y,U',V',g^{-1}\mathcal G)$ from $J^\bullet$, as in steps 4-6 of its proof; we use these. Since $g^{-1}$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], $g^{-1}(s):g^{-1}\mathcal G[0]\to g^{-1}I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $Q(g^{-1}(s))$ is invertible in the derived category and, $J^\bullet$ being K-injective, $-\circ g^{-1}(s):\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(g^{-1}I^\bullet,J^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Hom}_K(g^{-1}\mathcal G[0],J^\bullet)$ is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] (both Hom sets identified with Hom sets of $D$ by $Q$). Hence there is a morphism of complexes $\beta:g^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ with $\beta\circ g^{-1}(s)$ homotopic to $s'$. A homotopy between two morphisms $g^{-1}\mathcal G[0]\to J^\bullet$ consists of $h^0:g^{-1}\mathcal G\to J^{-1}=0$ and $h^n=0$ for $n\ne0$ (the source vanishes in degree $\ne0$), so it is zero: $\beta\circ g^{-1}(s)=s'$ exactly. Now apply clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] to $u=g$, $G=\mathcal G$ with $s$, $M^\bullet=J^\bullet$, $t=s'$ and this $\beta$ ($M^\bullet$ K-injective): $g^*=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))\circ\mathcal H^q(a\mapsto\beta(\eta_g(a)))$, where $\gamma$ is a lift of $\mathrm{id}_{g^{-1}\mathcal G}$ from $(J^\bullet,s')$ to the resolution used in [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], i.e. $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))$ is the identification $H^q(\mathrm{id})$ of [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent]. So, with $H^q(Y_{\Et},g^{-1}\mathcal G)$ computed from $s'$ (as in the Mayer-Vietoris sequence of $Y$), $g^*=\mathcal H^q(\varphi_X)$ with $\varphi_X:I^\bullet(X)\to J^\bullet(Y)$, $\varphi_X(a)=\beta(Y)(\eta_{g,I^\bullet}(X)(a))$, where $\eta_g$ is the unit of $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $(g_*g^{-1}I)(X)=(g^{-1}I)(Y)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

proof.text: *The maps on sections over the opens, and the morphism of short exact sequences of complexes.* For an open $W\subseteq X$ put $W'=g^{-1}(W)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with $S=X$, $V=W$, the whole of $Y$) $W\times_XY$ is the open subscheme $W'$ of $Y$, and for opens $W_1\subseteq W_2$ the base change of the inclusion is the inclusion $W_1'\subseteq W_2'$; so $(g_*H)(W)=H(W')$ for an abelian sheaf $H$ on $Y_{\Et}$, with restriction maps those of $H$ along $W_1'\subseteq W_2'$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Define $\varphi_W:I^\bullet(W)\to J^\bullet(W')$, $\varphi_W(a)=\beta(W')(\eta_{g,I^\bullet}(W)(a))$, for $W\in\{X,U,V,U\cap V\}$ (for $W=X$ this is the $\varphi_X$ of step 1; $X'=Y$, and $U'\cap V'=(U\cap V)'$). Each $\varphi_W$ is a morphism of complexes, since $\eta_{g,I^n}$ is natural in the sheaf [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $\beta$ is a morphism of complexes of sheaves. For $W_1\subseteq W_2$ and $a\in I^n(W_2)$, $\varphi_{W_1}(a|_{W_1})=\varphi_{W_2}(a)|_{W_1'}$, because $\eta_{g,I^n}:I^n\to g_*g^{-1}I^n$ and $\beta^n:g^{-1}I^n\to J^n$ are morphisms of sheaves, hence commute with the restriction maps (those of $g_*g^{-1}I^n$ being those of $g^{-1}I^n$ along $W_1'\subseteq W_2'$). Since $Y=U'\cup V'$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] (steps 2-4 of its proof, for $(Y,U',V')$ and the injective resolution $J^\bullet$) gives the short exact sequence of complexes $0\to J^\bullet(Y)\xrightarrow{a'}J^\bullet(U')\oplus J^\bullet(V')\xrightarrow{b'}J^\bullet(U'\cap V')\to0$, $a'(x)=(x|_{U'},x|_{V'})$, $b'(y,z)=y|_{U'\cap V'}-z|_{U'\cap V'}$, with the same sign convention as $0\to I^\bullet(X)\xrightarrow{a}I^\bullet(U)\oplus I^\bullet(V)\xrightarrow{b}I^\bullet(U\cap V)\to0$ on $X$. By the compatibility with restriction and additivity of $\varphi$: $a'\circ\varphi_X=(\varphi_U\oplus\varphi_V)\circ a$ and $b'\circ(\varphi_U\oplus\varphi_V)=\varphi_{U\cap V}\circ b$, i.e. $(\varphi_X,\varphi_U\oplus\varphi_V,\varphi_{U\cap V})$ is a morphism of short exact sequences of complexes.

proof.text: *Morphism of long exact sequences on the chain level.* By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] applied to the morphism of step 2, the maps $\mathcal H^q(\varphi_X)$, $\mathcal H^q(\varphi_U)\oplus\mathcal H^q(\varphi_V)$, $\mathcal H^q(\varphi_{U\cap V})$ form a morphism from the long exact cohomology sequence of $0\to I^\bullet(X)\to I^\bullet(U)\oplus I^\bullet(V)\to I^\bullet(U\cap V)\to0$ to that of $0\to J^\bullet(Y)\to J^\bullet(U')\oplus J^\bullet(V')\to J^\bullet(U'\cap V')\to0$: $\mathcal H^q(a')\mathcal H^q(\varphi_X)=(\mathcal H^q(\varphi_U)\oplus\mathcal H^q(\varphi_V))\mathcal H^q(a)$, $\mathcal H^q(b')(\mathcal H^q(\varphi_U)\oplus\mathcal H^q(\varphi_V))=\mathcal H^q(\varphi_{U\cap V})\mathcal H^q(b)$ and $\mathcal H^{q+1}(\varphi_X)\circ\delta^q=\delta'^q\circ\mathcal H^q(\varphi_{U\cap V})$ for all $q\ge0$ (using $\mathcal H^q$ of a direct sum of complexes is the direct sum).

proof.text: *Identification of $\mathcal H^q(\varphi_W)$ with $g_W^*$ for $W\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}$.* Let $j_W$, $j_{W'}$ be the open immersions, $g_W:W'\to W$ the restriction of $g$, $h=g\circ j_{W'}=j_W\circ g_W$, and $\kappa=c_{g,j_{W'}}^{-1}\circ c_{j_W,g_W}:g_W^{-1}j_W^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}$, natural in the sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]; $\kappa_{\mathcal G}$ is the isomorphism of the statement. Recall the identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] (step 6 of its proof): by clause 5 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], $j_W^{-1}(s):j_W^{-1}\mathcal G\to j_W^{-1}I^\bullet$ and $j_{W'}^{-1}(s'):j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}\mathcal G\to j_{W'}^{-1}J^\bullet$ are resolutions by bounded below complexes of injectives (K-injective), and $H^q(W_{\Et},\mathcal G|_W)=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}I^\bullet))\cong\mathcal H^q(I^\bullet(W))$, $H^q(W'_{\Et},(g^{-1}\mathcal G)|_{W'})=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(W',j_{W'}^{-1}J^\bullet))\cong\mathcal H^q(J^\bullet(W'))$ through the isomorphisms of complexes $\rho_{I^\bullet}(W)$, $\rho_{J^\bullet}(W')$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1). (a) *$g_W^*$ on the chain level.* Put $M^\bullet=j_{W'}^{-1}J^\bullet$ and $\beta_W=j_{W'}^{-1}(\beta)\circ\kappa_{I^\bullet}:g_W^{-1}j_W^{-1}I^\bullet\to j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}I^\bullet\to M^\bullet$. By naturality of $\kappa$ and step 1, $\beta_W\circ g_W^{-1}(j_W^{-1}(s))=j_{W'}^{-1}(\beta)\circ j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}(s)\circ\kappa_{\mathcal G}=j_{W'}^{-1}(s')\circ\kappa_{\mathcal G}=:t$, a quasi-isomorphism ($j_{W'}^{-1}(s')$ is one, $\kappa_{\mathcal G}$ an isomorphism). Clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (for $u=g_W$, the sheaf $j_W^{-1}\mathcal G$ with resolution $j_W^{-1}(s)$, and $M^\bullet$, $t$, $\beta_W$; $M^\bullet$ K-injective) shows that, with $H^q(W'_{\Et},g_W^{-1}j_W^{-1}\mathcal G)$ computed from $t$, $g_W^*=\mathcal H^q$ of $\psi_W:\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(W',M^\bullet)$, $\psi_W(x)=\beta_W(\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}I^\bullet}(W)(x))$ (the factor $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(\gamma))$ being the identification $H^q(\mathrm{id})$ [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent], as in step 1). (b) *The identification $H^q(\kappa_{\mathcal G})$.* From $(M^\bullet,t)$ to $(M^\bullet,j_{W'}^{-1}(s'))$, $\mathrm{id}_{M^\bullet}$ is a lift of $\kappa_{\mathcal G}$ ($\mathrm{id}\circ t=j_{W'}^{-1}(s')\circ\kappa_{\mathcal G}$), so $H^q(\kappa_{\mathcal G})$ is the identity of $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(W',M^\bullet))$ (definition of $H^q(\varphi)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]). Hence $H^q(\kappa_{\mathcal G})\circ g_W^*=\mathcal H^q(\psi_W)$ as a map $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}I^\bullet))\to\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(W',j_{W'}^{-1}J^\bullet))$. (c) *Comparison with $\varphi_W$.* For $x\in\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}I^n)$: $\rho_{J}(W')(\psi_W(x))=\rho_J(W')\bigl(j_{W'}^{-1}(\beta)(\kappa_I(\eta_{g_W}(x)))\bigr)=\beta(W')\bigl(\rho_{g^{-1}I}(W')(\kappa_I(\eta_{g_W}(x)))\bigr)$ by naturality of $\rho$ in the sheaf ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1), for $j_{W'}$ and $\beta^n:g^{-1}I^n\to J^n$, with $(g^{-1}I)|_{W'}(W')=(g^{-1}I)(W')$), and $\rho_{g^{-1}I}(W')(\kappa_I(\eta_{g_W}(x)))=\eta_{g,I}(W)(\rho_I(W)(x))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-restriction-pullback-unit] (for $F=I^n$). So $\rho_{J^\bullet}(W')\circ\psi_W=\varphi_W\circ\rho_{I^\bullet}(W)$, and under the identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris], $H^q(\kappa_{\mathcal G})\circ g_W^*=\mathcal H^q(\varphi_W)$, for every $q\ge0$.

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Under the identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] (step 6 of its proof), the maps of its sequence for $(X,U,V,\mathcal G)$ are $(\rho_U,\rho_V)=\mathcal H^q(a)$, $\rho-\rho=\mathcal H^q(b)$ and $\delta=\delta^q$, and those for $(Y,U',V',g^{-1}\mathcal G)$ are $\mathcal H^q(a')$, $\mathcal H^q(b')$, $\delta'^q$; by steps 1 and 4 the vertical maps $g^*$, $(H^q(\kappa_{\mathcal G})g_U^*)\oplus(H^q(\kappa_{\mathcal G})g_V^*)$, $H^q(\kappa_{\mathcal G})g_{U\cap V}^*$ are $\mathcal H^q(\varphi_X)$, $\mathcal H^q(\varphi_U)\oplus\mathcal H^q(\varphi_V)$, $\mathcal H^q(\varphi_{U\cap V})$. Step 3 says exactly that all squares commute, including $g^*\circ\delta=\delta'\circ H^q(\kappa_{\mathcal G})g_{U\cap V}^*$ (from degree $q$ on $U\cap V$ to degree $q+1$ on $Y$). The result is independent of the choices of $I^\bullet$, $J^\bullet$, $\beta$, since the maps $g^*$, $g_W^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (1) and the two sequences (step 1) are.
